macros.name: addlcword
macros.doc: Add a word to the list of designated “lower-case words” which will not be capitalized by \capitalizetitle.

macros.name: addlcwords
macros.doc: Add words to the list of designated “lower-case words” which will not be capitalized by \capitalizetitle.

macros.name: alphabetic
macros.doc: The command \alphabetic discards punctuation, symbols, and numerals, while retaining alphabetic characters and blankspaces.

macros.name: capitalize
macros.doc: The command \capitalize turns the first character of string into its upper case, if it is alphabetic.

macros.name: capitalizetitle
macros.doc: Makes every word of a multi-word input string capitalized, except for specifically noted “lower-case words” (examples might include prepositions, conjunctions, etc.).

macros.name: capitalizewords
macros.doc: The command \capitalizewords turns the first character of every word in string into its upper case, if it is alphabetic.

macros.name: caselower
macros.doc: The command \caselower takes the input string or token, and converts all uppercase characters in the string to lowercase.

macros.name: caseupper
macros.doc: The command \caseupper takes the input string or token, and converts all lowercase characters in the string to uppercase.

macros.name: changecase
macros.doc: The command \changecase switches lower case to upper case and upper case to lower case.

macros.name: convertchar
macros.doc: The command \convertchar is a substitution command in which a specified match character in the original string (from-char) is substituted with a different string (to-string).

macros.name: convertword
macros.doc: The command \convertword is a substitution command in which a specified match string in the original string (from-string) is substituted with a different string (to-string).

macros.name: decodetoken
macros.doc: The command \decodetoken deassigns the supplied token from the reserved stringstrings user variables (the optional argument dictates which user variable), so that the token may be used in the normal way again.

macros.name: defaultTreatments
macros.doc: The command \defaultTreatments resets all treatment modes to their default settings, which are to leave individual characters unaltered by a string manipulation.

macros.name: encodetoken
macros.doc: The command \encodetoken assigns the supplied token to one of three reserved stringstrings user variables (the optional argument dictates which user variable).

macros.name: findchars
macros.doc: The command \findchars checks to see if the character match-char occurs anywhere in string.

macros.name: findwords
macros.doc: The command \findwords checks to see if the string match-string occurs anywhere in string.

macros.name: getargs
macros.doc: The command \getargs mimics the Unix command of the same name, in that it parses string to determine how many arguments (i.e., words) are in string, and extracts each word into a separate variable.

macros.name: getaword
macros.doc: The command \getaword returns a word of string defined by the index, n. In this case, “word” is a sequence of characters delimited either by spaces or by the first or last characters of the string.

macros.name: getnextword
macros.doc: The command \getnextword returns the next word of string.

macros.name: gobblechar
macros.doc: The command \gobblechar returns a string in which the first character of string has been removed.

macros.name: gobblechars
macros.doc: The command \gobblechars returns a string in which the first n characters of string have been removed.

macros.name: isnextbyte
macros.doc: The command \isnextbyte tests to see if the first byte of string equals matchbyte.

macros.name: LB
macros.doc: \LB and \RB may be used within stringstrings arguments in lieu of grouping braces, if the final result is to be retokenized.

macros.name: noblanks
macros.doc: The command \noblanks removes blankspaces (both hard and soft) from a string, while leaving other characters unchanged.

macros.name: nosymbolsnumerals
macros.doc: The command \nosymbolsnumerals removes symbols and numerals from a string, while leaving other characters unchanged.

macros.name: RB
macros.doc: \LB and \RB may be used within stringstrings arguments in lieu of grouping braces, if the final result is to be retokenized.

macros.name: removeleadingspaces
macros.doc: The command \removeleadingspaces removes any leading spaces of the string.

macros.name: removeword
macros.doc: The command \removeword removes the first word of string, along with any of its leading and trailing spaces.

macros.name: resetlcwords
macros.doc: Removes all words from designated “lower-case words” list.

macros.name: retokenize
macros.doc: The command \retokenize takes a string that is encoded according to the stringstrings encoding scheme, and repopulates the encoded characters with their LaTeX tokens.

macros.name: reversestring
macros.doc: The command \reversestring reverses the sequence of characters in a string, such that what started as the first character becomes the last character in the manipulated string, and what started as the last character becomes the first character.

macros.name: rotateleadingspaces
macros.doc: The command \rotateleadingspaces takes any leading spaces of the string and rotates them to the end of the string.

macros.name: rotateword
macros.doc: The command \rotateword takes the first word of string (and its leading and trailing spaces) and rotates them to the end of the string.

macros.name: solelylowercase
macros.doc: The command \solelylowercase is similar to \caselower, except that all punctuation, numerals, and symbols are discarded from the string. Blankspaces are left alone, and uppercase characters are converted to lowercase.

macros.name: solelyuppercase
macros.doc: The command \solelyuppercase is similar to \caseupper, except that all punctuation, numerals, and symbols are discarded from the string. Blankspaces are left alone, and lowercase characters are converted to uppercase.

macros.name: stringdecode
macros.doc: The command \stringdecode returns a copy of the string that has been decoded.

macros.name: stringencode
macros.doc: The command \stringencode returns a copy of the string that has been encoded according to the stringstrings encoding scheme.

macros.name: stringlength
macros.doc: The command \stringlength returns the length of string in characters (not bytes).

macros.name: testalphabetic
macros.doc: The command \testalphabetic is used to ascertain whether all the characters in string are alphabetic or not.

macros.name: testcapitalized
macros.doc: The command \testcapitalized is used to ascertain whether the first character of string is capitalized or not.

macros.name: testleadingalpha
macros.doc: The command \testleadingalpha is used to ascertain whether the first character of string is alphabetic.

macros.name: testlowercase
macros.doc: The command \testlowercase is used to ascertain whether all the alphabetic characters in string are lowercase or not.

macros.name: testmatchingchar
macros.doc: The command \testmatchingchar is used to ascertain whether character n of string equals match-char or not.

macros.name: testsolelylowercase
macros.doc: The command \testsolelylowercase is used to ascertain whether all the characters in string are lowercase or not.

macros.name: testsolelyuppercase
macros.doc: The command \testsolelyuppercase is used to ascertain whether all the characters in string are uppercase or not.

macros.name: testuncapitalized
macros.doc: The command \testuncapitalized is used to ascertain whether the first character of string is uncapitalized.

macros.name: testuppercase
macros.doc: The command \testuppercase is used to ascertain whether all the alphabetic characters in string are uppercase or not.
